# Fable holistic review: story and faction lore, main at 2b15e9f5a

Ryan, Nov 24 2026: "use a fable review to do a holistic pass at the story/faction lore".

## What to do
Read the whole story and faction text the game ships (the files below are the live sources; anything under docs/archive is history) and give Ryan a holistic pass:
1. Does each of the six factions have a clear, distinct identity (who they are, what they want, how they talk), and does it hold the same across voices, rival lines, situations, titles, the campaign tables and the faction playbook? Faction ids never change; display names do (rename_map_final.md). Flag any old display name or retired term still in player-facing text.
2. Contradictions: facts, names, ranks, history or motives that disagree between files.
3. The story arc: does the campaign read as one story with a beginning, rising stakes and an ending? Where does it sag, repeat or go unexplained?
4. Tone and writing: lines that are flat, too long for a battle log, repetitive, or that break the voice of their faction. Quote a few of the best and worst.
5. Gaps: factions, admirals, events or endings that have little or no text compared with the others.
Then give your top 8 recommendations, most valuable first, each one sentence on what to change and where. Do not rewrite whole files; short example lines are fine.

# Voidsworn: rules for any AI agent (Claude or another model)

**The game.** Embers of the Hollow Sun (repo name voidsworn) is a hex fleet-tactics roguelite. The product is the Godot 4 game in
`godot/`, played on Ryan's Windows PC only. Godot is the only rules source: the browser rules files at the repo root are retired, frozen history, and CI checks Godot against its own saved results (RULEBOOK 3.1, R405, Nov 22 2026).
The owner is Ryan. He is not a coder: he judges work by pictures. Faction ids never change; their display names do
(contrib/opus/compute/rename_map_final.md): `voidsworn` = Sunward Crusade, `corsair` = Ashfall Hullbreakers, `ithar` = the
Glasswrights, `deathless` = Eclipse, `chorus` = the Chorus, `hegemony` = Meridian Directorate.

**Read first.**
1. `docs/RULEBOOK.md`: every rule in force, each with its reason. **It wins** over this file and every older doc (its section 0.3
   says which document wins after it). Sections 3.5 to 9 live in four files under `.claude/rules/` (pc-harness, ships,
   godot-battle, godot-ui); they are plain Markdown and part of the rulebook for every seat, not only Claude (issue 1660).
2. HANDOFF.md section 0 and contrib/opus/LOOP.md ("The seats", the LATEST lines): what is running now. They win for status only.
3. The playbook for your area: `docs/playbooks/` (PROGRAM.md first).
4. contrib/opus/FINDINGS.md is the dated history of rulings, not the live source. Anything under `docs/archive/` is history:
   never follow it.

Auditing from outside? Follow `docs/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` exactly (RULEBOOK 2.11) and the brief in your issue.
Artoo (Ryan's ChatGPT dot) reviews on its own, technical problems only, each comment marked "Artoo (technical review):"
and naming the commit it read; general sweeps go on issue 906 (RULEBOOK 2.7, R295).

## The job board (Ryan, Nov 2 2026; RULEBOOK 2.4)

- Every job is an open GitHub issue: https://github.com/rcbailey12/voidsworn/issues. The label says who has it: `codex` (Codex on
  Ryan's PC), `muse` (Rey and its models), `opus` (Claude), `ryan` (waiting on Ryan), plus `neon` (Neon, R363) and `blocked`. Who does which kind of
  work is RULEBOOK 2.6; which seats are live today is LOOP.md "The seats".
- Agents deliver by pushing a branch named `codex/issue-<number>`, `muse/issue-<number>`, `work/issue-<number>` (or
  `work/issue-<number>-<arm>`), `opus/issue-<number>` or `neon/issue-<number>` (Neon, R363). Any other one-level `muse/<name>` branch also gets a pull request (Nov 17 audit);
  Muse names a scratch branch `muse/wip-<name>` to keep it out. Never push to main (R75); the only exception is LOOP.md and
  FINDINGS.md, which the Board commits straight to main (R102).
- The push makes GitHub open the pull request by itself (.github/workflows/auto_pr.yml, for those branch shapes) and run the
  checks once (.github/workflows/checks.yml: standing checks, no em dashes in changed files, Godot rules parity, Godot game
  checks; a docs-only push skips the Godot jobs, "All checks" is the one mark to read, a conflict with main fails, RULEBOOK
  12.3). A branch with any other name gets no automatic checks: open its pull request by hand, then start them by hand
  (Actions tab, "checks", "Run workflow"; or `gh workflow run checks.yml --ref <branch>`). The Board reviews and merges;
  nobody merges their own pull request (RULEBOOK 2.2).
- Codex runs locally on the PC only, in up to four lanes (RULEBOOK 2.7, R301; no cloud tasks: their model cannot be pinned, R268). The Board launches each Codex job itself through the PC queue (LOOP.md
  "The seats" says how), and every `codex` issue also carries `blocked`, so the old board watcher (tools/pc/codex_board.bat)
  cannot run it a second time.
- Every issue opens with this fixed block, so any agent can pick it up without asking:
  ```
  Owner: codex | muse | opus
  Brief: <path to the brief, or "below">
  Deliver to: <folder or files>
  Branch: <agent>/issue-<number>
  Base: <branch>
  Effort (Codex): high | xhigh   or   Models (Muse): <set>
  Done when: <the check that proves it, and what Ryan will see>
  ```
  Muse's Models line for research, design and review jobs: Rey writes a blind leg first, DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok and Flash each
  write a leg, Rey chairs (R89, R231, RULEBOOK 2.8). Muse's standing instructions: `contrib/opus/briefs/muse_standing_rule.md`.
- Use the optional Base line for an earlier branch the job needs. The runner merges `origin/<branch>` and commits the
  merge before the agent starts; a conflict stops the run with the checkout kept. Briefs never ask the agent to merge.
  The PC runners set the running label and one status comment per job branch, edit it on retries and at the end, and
  clear the label at the end. GitHub reporting failures are logged and never fail the job (RULEBOOK 2.4, issue 846).
- Ship concept and build issues carry an "Approved pick:" line copied from the fleet list (docs/ship_pipeline/FLEET.md;
  `node contrib/opus/tools/fleet_list.js --pick "faction|Class"`), so no brief goes out without Ryan's earlier pick (issue 1421).
- Ship build issues add four lines to the block (Ryan, Nov 11 2026, R214; template in docs/playbooks/ships.md section 7):
  Route per part, Inside, Paint stack, Budget. Every build pull request body carries its done-when evidence and a method line
  (build sheet link, manifest, budget numbers, changes made to the sheet); the outside check (issue 256) returns a build PR
  without them as BLOCKING (RULEBOOK 5.14).
- One current instruction per job: the current run brief sits at the top of the issue body under the fixed block, older
  runs marked done. The PC runner reads the body only; a brief in a comment never reaches the worker (R281, RULEBOOK 2.4).
- Before queueing or relabelling an issue, check for a merged pull request that names it; issues stay open after merges
  here, so open is not proof of undone work. Close an issue in the same step as its merge when its scope is done
  (R288, RULEBOOK 2.4).
- Claim before you run: a seat starting a job sets the running label and its status comment first (RULEBOOK 2.4). If a
  job is already claimed, or its delivery branch already exists, do not run it; tell the Board. Two seats ran issue 872
  on the same morning because nothing enforced the owner label.
- **A ruling lands with its document.** A ruling that changes a working method is not landed until the same pull request edits
  the rulebook or the working document a worker reads for that area (the playbook, RECIPE.md, this file) (R214, RULEBOOK 0.2).
  Its FINDINGS row says "landed in <repo path>" or "one-off job decision"; the memory lint fails it otherwise (R291).
- Commits say "Refs #N", never a GitHub closing word before an issue number; use `gh api` REST, never GraphQL (RULEBOOK 2.5).

## Agent skills (issue 1658)

Skills for every seat live in `.agents/skills/` (copied to `.claude/skills/` by `node contrib/opus/tools/sync_skills.js`);
read `.agents/skills/README.md` first, its house notes win over the skill text. Issue tracker: `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
Domain words: `GLOSSARY.md`; decisions are RULEBOOK rules and FINDINGS rows, never ADRs (`docs/agents/domain.md`).

## If you are not the main agent: work in your own folder (RULEBOOK 2.12)

- Put everything you make in `contrib/<your-agent-name>/`. Do not edit files outside it: no game source, no tools, no docs, no
  `hulls*/` assets. Muse is the exception: it may deliver low-code fixes in text, data, tests, tools and docs as pull requests
  (R81).
- Proposing a change to an existing file? Put a copy of the whole changed file in your folder at the same relative path, plus a
  `NOTES.md` that says what changed and why. Reviews go in `contrib/<your-agent-name>/reviews/<topic>.md`.
- The Board merges what works. See `contrib/README.md`.

## Owner preferences that apply to any agent (RULEBOOK section 1)

- Plain words, short, lead with the answer, give your pick and why; no em dashes; no human-hour estimates (estimate in agent
  runs and review rounds, from the board's own history).
- Pictures for anything visual: one per item, its code name on it, no taller than 720 px.
- Anything Ryan runs himself is a double-click `.bat` file (Windows 10, PowerShell 5.1, no Python of his own).
- Before anything bigger than a quick fix, ask 3 to 5 plain multiple-choice scope questions in one batch.
- Questions for Ryan go to him in your own chat, never as GitHub tags or comments; message him only when something lands or
  needs him. Non-urgent picks wait for the Morning or Evening Pick Sheet (RULEBOOK 1.8, R408).
- No paid OpenAI API review where Artoo or Claude code review covers the PR (2.18, R406); no GPU capture on a PR before green
  checks and a passed review (3.12, R407).
- Heavy work (AI models, Blender, Godot captures) runs on Ryan's PC through the queue. GPU work is sized to the job and to
  what the RTX 5080 can hold, not a fixed job count (R293, RULEBOOK 3.4); frame-time measurements claim the GPU solo, lane C
  stays code only, and gpu_go.txt still wins.
  Keep your PC folder lean. Deleting on his PC follows RULEBOOK 3.3: jobs and the cleanup janitor may remove their own
  rebuildable leftovers under its safe rules; nothing else is deleted without Ryan's yes.

`CLAUDE.md` is a short pointer to this file plus Claude-only notes. Keep the two in step. The fuller AGENTS.md of Nov 8 to 11
(seat table, ship sections, PC notes) is archived at docs/archive/AGENTS_2026-11-11.md; every rule it held is in the rulebook.

## File: godot/story/README.md
```
# godot/story: admiral lines, flagship names, titles, career and (later) the faction arcs

Owner: the story and career stream (travel sprint, R37). Folders: `godot/story/` (data, text, logic) and `godot/ui/career/` (screens). This file is the contract with the campaign (G3) and the game shell and battle scene (G2). A change to it lands here in the same commit.

**Rules this layer keeps:**
- It never calls `campaign.act()` and never touches the rules PRNG, so campaign parity and battle parity cannot see it. `story_test.gd` checks that a whole run plays out the same with and without the story attached.
- Career data lives in its own file, `user://voidsworn_career.json` (plus `.bak`), not in the campaign save.
- The one write into the campaign is the flagship's name (`ship.name`), and only when the player renames it.

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `story.gd` | The layer itself (a Node). Watches the campaign, records battles and runs, gives lines for text boxes, renames the flagship, opens the screens. |
| `career.gd` | The career profile: records per admiral, totals, medals, titles, run history. Pure logic, no nodes. |
| `battle_voice.gd` | Admiral, enemy flagship and Nemesis lines in battle, driven by the rules' event stream. |
| `rival.gd` | The Nemesis's voice (R42): picks his lines by faction, personality, scars and how you beat him; his beat 1 calling card; his beat 3 hail by the run's lean. |
| `tokens.gd` | Story tokens (`{rival}`, `{he}` `{him}` `{his}`, `{rival_deed}`, `{first_lost}` ...) with plain fallbacks. |
| `arc.gd` | The arc engine: beat data, variant pick, conditional lines, event-shaped cards, endings. Arc files come after approval. |
| `data/voices.json` | 24 admirals x 11 moments, and enemy sector flagship lines per faction. |
| `data/rival_lines.json` | The Nemesis's pools per faction: hail, rematch, final, beaten, death, gloat, kill, signature, scars, memory (7 ways you beat him), 6 personalities, calling cards, beat 3 hails. |
| `data/titles.json` | 12 titles earned from how you fight, plus a fallback, each worded per faction, with the rules in plain words. |
| `data/medals.json` | 12 medals. |
| `data/arcs.json` | What finishing each arc pays: medal, arc title, flagship paint, and the hull unlock id. |
| `outlines.md`, `outlines_variants.md` | The six faction story outlines, rewritten Oct 31 to the approved lore round 8 (R59; same beats, flags and effects), and their B versions, skims and rival incidents. |
| `unlocks.md` | Draft hull unlock per faction, for stream B (rules and balance). |
| `test/story_test.gd` | Headless checks (below). `test/check_outlines.py` checks outline word counts, pronoun tokens and dashes. `test/fixture_arc.json` is test data for `arc.gd`. |
| `../ui/career/career_screen.gd` | The Career screen: Records, Medals, Titles, History, Chronicle tabs. |
| `../ui/career/rename_dialog.gd` | "Name your flagship". |
| `../ui/career/crest.gd` | Faction crests and medals drawn as vector strokes (crests instead of portraits). Usable anywhere. |

## Hooks wanted from other streams

Each hook is a few lines, guarded so the game still runs if `godot/story/` is missing. Until a hook lands, that part of step 1 just does not show.

**Status (Oct 26):** hooks 1, 2 and 4 are in (commit 7c704d9, added by the story stream as clearly marked "story hook" lines in `campaign_host.gd`, `battle.gd` and `title.gd`; G2 owns those files and may move them). Hook 3 (G3's campaign screens) and the arc beat hook (below, "Story arcs") are still wanted. The rename prompt and career recording already work through hook 1.

### 1. Campaign host (G2, `godot/main/campaign_host.gd`, in `start()`, before `ui.bind(C)`)

```gdscript
# story layer (godot/story/README.md): admiral lines, flagship name, titles, career records
var story = null
if ResourceLoader.exists("res://story/story.gd"):
	story = load("res://story/story.gd").new()
	story.name = "Story"
	add_child(story)
	story.attach(C, not bot)      # bot runs keep the career in memory only
```

Attaching before `ui.bind(C)` makes the story see each `changed` signal before the UI draws, so any line it offers is ready for that draw. In bot runs, attach it too (it records into memory only), so every full-run bot run also tests the story layer.

Then pass the story into battles, for example `main.play_api(a, {"bot": bot, "can_retreat": C.can_retreat(), "story": story})`.

### 2. Battle scene (G2, `godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd`)

```gdscript
var voice = null   # story layer (godot/story/battle_voice.gd)

# in _begin(a), after V = api.view():
if opts_story != null:    # the "story" option from play_api, or res://story/battle_voice.gd loaded directly
	voice = opts_story.battle_voice()
	voice.setup_from_rules(R, V)
	for l in voice.opening(): hud.add_log(l["text"], l["kind"])

# at the top of _play_event(e):
if voice != null:
	for l in voice.on_event(e): hud.add_log(l["text"], l["kind"])

# in _end_flow(), before hud.show_end(...):
if voice != null:
	var vl: String = voice.closing(win)
	if vl != "": body += "\n\n" + vl
```

Lines go to the existing battle log, with existing colour classes (`"s"` gilt for your admiral, `"e"` red for the enemy). The voice also works in quick battles: `load("res://story/battle_voice.gd").new()` needs no campaign.

What it says, once per battle each: the opening (your admiral; against a sector flagship, its hail first; against the Nemesis, his hail first, his final line in sector III), your flagship below 40% hull, your first ship lost, your Command, the enemy flagship destroyed (its last words, then your admiral), and on the end card your admiral's win or loss line (or the Nemesis's gloat if he beat you).

### 3. Campaign screens (G3, `godot/ui/campaign/campaign_ui.gd`)

The UI can find the story at `get_parent().get_node_or_null("Story")` (the host adds it as a sibling) and asks for one line for the screen it is drawing:

```gdscript
var st = get_parent().get_node_or_null("Story")
var line: String = st.campaign_line() if st != null else ""
if line != "": v.add_child(lbl(line, 17, GILT))     # plain text, no BBCode
```

| Screen | `campaign_line()` gives |
|---|---|
| page `admiral` | the picked admiral's pick line |
| modal `intro` and `sector` | your admiral's sector line |
| page `end` | your admiral's win or loss line, then "Title earned: ..." on a new line |

Also available:
- `st.titled_name(admiral_id)`: "Warlord Grax Ironmaw the Render" (the latest title earned), for the admiral card and the map sidebar.
- `st.open_rename()`: opens "Name your flagship" (a "Rename" button on the fleet screen's flagship card would call this). The story already opens it once by itself over the first sector intro of every run.
- `st.open_career()`: opens the Career screen (a "Career" tab beside the Progression tabs would call this).
- Signals `st.medal_earned(id, name)` and `st.title_earned(row)`, for a toast if wanted.

### 4. Title screen (G2, `godot/main/title.gd`)

```gdscript
if ResourceLoader.exists("res://story/story.gd"):
	menu.add_child(_button("Career", func() -> void: load("res://story/story.gd").open_standalone(self)))
```

## What is recorded

Per battle, from the rules' own `B` after `finish_battle` (no new rules fields): enemy ships destroyed, your ships lost (squadrons and captured prizes not counted), and `B.usage` (guns fired by kind and arc, aimed shots, rams, boardings, captures, orders, abilities, Commands).

Per run, at the end screen: the title earned, the run's line in the history, the admiral's record (runs, wins, best sector, battles, kills, losses, titles, flagship names) and the totals.

**Titles** (`data/titles.json`, rules in plain words in each row): brawler (rams and boardings), prize taker (captures), lancer (lance and null share; the rules id is still `gauss`), torpedoer, carrier, broadside (port and starboard share), gunline (battery share), marksman (aimed shots), anvil (braces), unscarred (battles with no loss), butcher (kills per battle), tactician (abilities per battle). A run needs 3 battles. The strongest score wins; otherwise the fallback (the Steadfast).

**Medals** (`data/medals.json`): First Blood, Flagship Breaker, Lightning Strike, Last Stand, Unbroken, Prize Master, Nemesis Slain, Victor, Against the Odds, Centurion, Long Service, Six Banners.

## Story arcs (step 3, after Ryan approves `outlines.md`)

The plumbing is built and tested (`arc.gd`, `tokens.gd`, `rival.gd`); the arc files (`data/arcs/<faction>.json`) are written once Ryan approves the text.

- `story.arc_beat(n)` returns the card for beat 1, 2 or 3 of the run's faction as an event-shaped dictionary, `{id, t, b, o:[{k, l, s, r, fl, need?}], outs, skim, skim_first, charge, variant, arc: true}`: the same shape as `EVENTS` in data.js, so the existing event screen can draw it and the existing `applyOutcome` and `eventFlags` apply it (each option's story flag rides in `fl`, so `RUN.flags` remembers it). `outs[k]` is the one-sentence result to show after the click. `skim_first` says to open on the short card.
- After the campaign applies the choice: `story.arc_chose(card, key)` (marks the variant seen, keeps the choice for the Chronicle). After beat 3's fight: `story.arc_end(won)` (Chronicle, medal, title, paint, unlock id).
- Outcome keys used by the outlines: `cred`, `cost`, `relic`, `payRelic`, `xp`, `healAll`, `dmgAll`, `dmgOne`, `dmgBig`, `shipRaw` (+`vet`), `mod`, `payMod`, `payXp`, `nemIntel`, `nemClock`, `ambush`. Counters written for the rival's memory: `mercy`, `greed`, `loud`.
- **Hook wanted (G3 with stream B):** show `story.arc_beat(1)` after the sector I intro, and `arc_beat(2)` and `arc_beat(3)` when sectors II and III begin, through the event screen. Until then the arcs do not appear.
- **Stream B's Nemesis (R42, now in data.js):** the story reads `RUN.nem.persona` (stream B's eight ids, four per faction; `test/check_personas.py` checks the pools match `NEM_FAC`), `beat` (how you beat him; `broad` maps to battery, `ion` to lance, `evaded` to evasive), `epithet` (part of his full name), `scars` and `beaten`. Still asked: a gender field on `RUN.nem` (`g`: `m`, `f` or `n`; until then `tokens.gd` guesses from feminine names in the pools, and a Chorus rival is `it`); `beaten`, `scars`, `persona`, `beat` and `epithet` carried into the battle's `B.nem`; and an event `{t: "nem_signature"}` when his faction behaviour fires, so the battle voice can speak it.
- **Arc end rule:** close the arc on his sector III fight; if he is restored (Eclipse, rules field `revive`), on the second fight. If he flees or withdraws, the win still finishes the arc, with the escape line from outlines.md.

## Checks

```
godot --headless --path godot --script res://story/test/story_test.gd [-- runs]
python3 godot/story/test/check_outlines.py
```

`story_test.gd`: data complete (24 admirals x 11 moments, faction and Nemesis lines, titles worded for all six factions, no em dashes); 14 hand-made runs earn the expected titles; career records, medals, save, load and backup fallback; the battle voice on scripted events and on a real rules battle played by the game's AI; whole campaign runs with the story attached, recorded, and the campaign state identical with and without it.

## File: godot/story/outlines.md
```
# Embers of the Hollow Sun: six faction story arcs

Status: **human-voiced rewrite aligned with the Nov 21 2026 narrative, space-first, and IP audits** (`contrib/opus/compute/lore_bible_r8.md`). Three beats per faction, the rival is the run's Nemesis, every choice is read again later, beat 3 is a story decision with a cost, finishing an arc pays a cosmetic reward and a hull unlock (`unlocks.md`), and every faction's road ends at the Hollow Sun.

Companion file: `outlines_variants.md` holds a second version of every beat, the short "skim" cards for later runs, and the shared rival incidents.

Flag ids (`vs_hand`, `hg_offbook`, `cs_party`, `it_song`, `dd_writ` and the rest) are kept intact so nothing downstream has to change.

## What each faction wants at the Hollow Sun

| Faction | Arc | Why they go sunward |
|---|---|---|
| Sunward Crusade | The Oath at the Hollow Sun | Burn out the siphon relay stealing the Vesper Reach's light. |
| Meridian Directorate | Registry Order 41 | Secure the Hollow Sun orbital perimeter and catalog the surviving Lattice cores. |
| Ashfall Hullbreakers | Rook's Trail | Track down R-5 Rook in the wreck field and claim it: strongest keeps it. |
| The Chorus | Consume the Cores | Devour the surviving Lattice cores at Ardent's rim and finish the war Memory recalls. |
| The Glasswrights | The Last Lens | Recover the Lattice's last primary lens before Eclipse mounts it on a stolen star. |
| Eclipse | The Homecoming | Bring the remaining cores home and ignite Ardent's successor at the system's core. |

## How an arc works

- Three beats, one per sector, each a 100 to 150 word card with a choice. A one-line charge sits above beat 1.
- Every option shows its effect up front and gives one outcome sentence after the click.
- Effects used: credits, repairs, experience, salvage (the item type), a ship joining, a refit, hull damage, the Nemesis clock, one weakness reveal per arc at most, an ambush. Every choice writes a flag and may add to the shared counters stream B reads (mercy, greed, loud).
- Beat 3 is shown as sector III begins; the arc closes on the result of the sector III fight. Winning finishes the arc: medal, Chronicle entry, arc title, flagship paint, hull unlock. A win where the rival escapes still finishes the arc and adds one line in your faction's voice:
  - Sunward Crusade: *{rival} slipped clear into the dark. Chalk {his} hull code under the line.*
  - Meridian Directorate: *{rival} withdrew in good order. The dossier remains open.*
  - Ashfall Hullbreakers: *{rival} broke clamps and ran. We have {his} transponder signature now.*
  - The Chorus: *{He} fled into the cold. Our spores keep {his} drive signature.*
  - The Glasswrights: *{rival} withdrew along the glare line. There will be another pass.*
  - Eclipse: *{rival} broke contact. The Archive holds {his} last vector.*
- `[brackets]` are lines that show only when their condition holds; at most two show on a card. The checker (`godot/story/test/check_outlines.py`) measures each card at its shortest and longest.

**What a Chronicle entry records** (Career screen): the faction and arc, the rival's full name and faction, the three choices in their own words, whether you won, your first lost ship, and the title earned that run.

---

## 1. Sunward Crusade: "The Oath at the Hollow Sun"

Charge: *Push sunward, burn out whatever's draining Vesper's stars, and make sure the people who paid for the jump aren't forgotten.*

### Beat 1 (sector I): The Ember Shard
Your fleet holds orbit over Vesper's outer belt, where the core Seren drifted after the collapse and gave the Reach its first real plasma coils. Before the jump clocks hit zero, every captain chalks one name on the flagship's outer hull so nobody gets erased like Meridian erased the Reach. {best_captain} steps up first. [Prior loss: two captains chalk {fallen_name} from the last expedition lost.] Then the belt wardens hail with worse news: {rival} hit their forge station six hours ago. {rival_deed} They left one warm shard of Seren's casing sitting untouched on the loading bay, like a dare. The wardens want it carried sunward; your quartermasters want it sold before it pulls {rival} straight onto your wake.

- **Carry the shard sunward.** Gain salvage: the ember shard. {rival} tracks its thermal ping: Nemesis clock moves on 1. (flag `vs_hand`)
  *The wardens seal the warm shard inside a lead quench-box and bolt it into your flagship's bay.*

# Embers of the Hollow Sun: story variants, skims and rival incidents (round 8)

Companion to `outlines.md` (read that first). Rewritten Oct 31 2026 to the approved lore (`lore_bible_r8.md`, R59), with the same flags and effects as the round 3 drafts.

## How variants work

- Every beat has two versions, A (in outlines.md) and B (here). A run draws one version per beat, preferring the one this profile has seen less. Both versions set the **same flags** with the **same effects**, so beat 2 and beat 3 read beat 1 the same way whichever version you saw; only the situation and the option labels change.
- **Skim cards:** after a player has finished an arc twice, each beat opens on its skim card (40 words or fewer) with the same choices, and "Read in full" one click away.
- **Prior win:** if the Chronicle holds a win with this faction, beat 1 shows a one-line nod instead of the prior-loss line. Both lines apply to version A and version B; on a B card that is already long, they replace its last sentence before the choice.
- **Rival incidents:** twelve short cards about the Nemesis, usable by any player faction, written in his faction's terms. They are ordinary events (stream B's event deck), at most one per sector.

## 3. The three open code questions, answered from the code

**Q1. Can a Chorus commander be the Nemesis? YES.**
- The run's foes are every faction but your own, shuffled. JS: core.js:322, `foes:shuffle(RUN_FACTIONS.filter(f=>f!==fac))`. Godot: campaign.gd:945, `var foes = shuffle(RUN_FACTIONS.filter(func(f): return f != fac))`.
- The Nemesis takes `foes[3]`. JS: campaign_run.js:246, `const fac=(RUN.foes&&RUN.foes[3])||...`. Godot: campaign.gd:1516 `newNemesis`, ported by G3 in 34d1bfa.
- Stream B's R42 `NEM_FAC.chorus` has titles "Matriarch", "Elder Throat", "Hive-mind", "Brood-queen", so fix 7 was required.
- **Side fact:** sectors I to III use `foes[0..2]` (core.js:250, `RUN.foes[s-1]`), so the Nemesis's faction is never one of the three sector factions you fight.

**Q2. Does anything follow Beat 3? YES. And Beat 3 does not always end him.**
- **The run goes on:** Beat 3 shows as sector III begins. His fight is at column 4 at the latest. A rest stop (shipyard, drydock or field) and the sector flagship follow, and the run ends only on that flagship (citations in section 1).
- **He can survive sector III** (campaign_run.js:279-286 `nemAfterBattle`):
  - he flees: `if(o.fled){ ... out.push(... breaks off and runs ...)`;
  - a Deathless rival reassembles once: `else if(flagDead&&beh.revive&&!N.revived){ N.revived=true; ... if(RUN.sector>=3) N.met=RUN.sector-1; ...` (he comes for you again in sector III);
  - he withdraws when his flagship survives: `else out.push(... withdraws to fight another day.)`;
  - only `else if(flagDead&&RUN.sector>=3){ N.dead=true; ...` ends him.
- **What I changed:** outlines.md now closes the arc on his sector III fight (on the second fight if he reassembled). A win where he escapes still finishes the arc and adds one line in your faction's voice ("If he escaped" list under "How an arc works"). The README states this rule for the arc-end hook.

**Q3. Does the built game add variation beyond the outlines? YES, in design and in plumbing; outcomes stay fixed.**
- Two versions of every beat: outlines_variants.md, with arc.gd `pick_variant` preferring the one this profile has seen less.
- Calling cards by his faction and persona (24); his lines picked from pools by a stable hash of his name, the moment and a seed (rival.gd; presentation only, never the rules PRNG).
- Conditional lines from flags and run facts; skim cards after two finished arcs; Chronicle callbacks across runs.
- Choice outcomes are fixed and stated, as in the event system today; there are no hidden dice.
- The per-faction arc files (`godot/story/data/arcs/<faction>.json`) are built only after Ryan's read, as the B5 gate requires.

```
# Faction theme sheets (ships)

Issue 405, the ships track of docs/playbooks/PROGRAM.md. Written by the Board (Fable 5.2), Nov 10 2026, from the approved lore
(contrib/opus/compute/lore_bible_r8.md, the Look section of each faction), the 36 concepts in docs/ship_pipeline/concepts/, and
the owner's ship rulings in AGENTS.md. One sheet per faction. A concept, a three-view sheet (contrib/muse/design/concept_standard_2026_11/standard.md),
a hull build and a blob sweep are all judged against the sheet for that faction.

Ryan, Nov 10 2026, 18:44 CST: "all the factions shapes and stuff came before we redesigned them so I think it's worth just a full
update and pass based on the current faction lore and story". And earlier the same day: "I think all the concepts need reworking.
Hegemony and Sunward aren't TERRIBLY off, hullbreakers is okay but glasswrights, eclipse and chorus all need serious work. We wanted
to prove the building pipeline worked first and then redo all the concepts and builds." So every concept in
docs/ship_pipeline/concepts/ is history, not a target. The sheets below state what holds for each faction whatever direction is
picked; the section "The concept redo" at the end gives three directions per faction for Ryan to pick from.

Ryan, Nov 10 2026 (R164), on hard points: "It should vary by size of ship, faction, etc. We want things to be on theme."

## Rules for every faction

- Space ships, not sea ships (owner, Oct 22 and Oct 24). No keels or keel fins, raked stems, porthole rows, lattice masts,
  cranes, crossbar masts, funnels, railings or stepped yacht decks. Use the space version: flat armoured bellies with chines,
  sensor housings, antenna arrays, heat radiators, engine bells, docking hatches.
- No gun faces backward at rest; a turret may turn aft only to follow a target its arc allows (RULEBOOK 4.2, R222). Bow guns face forward, side guns face out.
- Matched symmetric pairs at sensible hard points, on visible mounts. The Hullbreakers are the one exception.
- The ship must read at the battle camera (camera 170): one clear silhouette, one main colour, one accent light. Detail that
  only shows up close is a bonus, never the identity.
- Every hull has real thickness and comprehensive insides through the whole hull: decks, frames, spaces and machinery, so a
  hit, break or death never shows an empty husk (R98, R209, R215). Ryan, Nov 11: "Let's ensure we're keeping in mind the
  hits, the breaks, the deaths and everything that affects the internals of the ship so we don't run into the issues of before
  with just empty looking husks". Chorus hulls carry flesh, bone and organs; Glasswrights layered glass and light.
- Breaks look blown apart, never sliced (R186; Ryan: "It's like straight lines and even halves. It doesn't feel like an
  explosion or major hit happened"). The faction's "How it breaks" line says where the hull gives way, not that it parts
  cleanly.
- Squadron craft are per faction (R253, Ryan, Nov 14: "Own models per faction"): each launching faction has its own
  fighter-role and bomber-role model in its own shape language (contrib/muse/design/squadrons_2026_11/), never one shared
  shape repainted.
- Hard points are not a fixed count (R164). Gun and engine points come from the hull's own weapon slots and engines. Breach
  anchors (where the hull opens when it dies) scale with class and follow the faction's own way of breaking, below.

### Breach anchors by class (the base count; each faction's sheet says how they are placed)

| Class | Base breach anchors | Authored break lines |
|---|---|---|
| Escort, frigate | 2 | 1 |
| Destroyer | 3 | 2 |
| Cruiser | 4 | 2 |
| Capital, carrier, barge | 6 | 3 |
| Flagship, station | 8 | 3 or 4 |

A faction may add or remove one where its sheet says so. tools/recipe/check_export.py reads the expected count from the hull's
class and faction (issue 363), never from a constant.

---

## Sunward Crusade (`voidsworn`)

**In one line:** a black iron blade with burning spires.

- **Silhouette:** long, narrow dagger or spearhead, widest at the stern third. A row of tall radiator spires along the spine,
  tallest amidships. Symmetric. The spires stand at about 70 percent of the concept table heights, with the same count,
  stations and profiles, and the ember shows in the fin slats, never as a whole lit tower: every Sunward build makes them
  with the one shared spire option, `radiator(..., glow='slats')` in tools/blender/kits/voidsworn/parts.py: the heat
  core glows ember the full height of the column and dark iron ribs, 0.15 apart, cross it, so the glow shows between the
  ribs as on the concepts; the fins themselves never glow. Why: Ryan, Nov 19 2026 (R331), on the Sunward concepts: "can we
  scale down the giant radiator/orange towers on each ship a bit too?"; S8 first (issue 1158), then Warden, Vigil, Harrow,
  Hearth and Bastion (R333). Ryan, Nov 20 2026, on the Warden's lit fins reading as copper: "fix ember glow" (issue 1156).
  The ember is bright: the whole core sits near the tip's level (stack.py SPIRE, root .70 of the tip), the tip still under
  the 0.8 glow threshold. Why: Ryan, Nov 20 2026 13:43 UTC, on S8 in game beside a brighter mock-up: "A bit brighter".
- **Shape language:** forged, heavy, vertical. Recessed lateral weapon galleries in long straight rows. Big engine bells. Plate with rivet
  lines, never rust.
- **Colours:** black iron, frost-white markings, bright ember (windows, engines, and the spires, which glow because they shed
  the reactor's heat).
- **Guns sit:** in armored flank casemates along both sides, plus one heavy pair at the bow. Manual optical fire-control blisters and recessed gun ports,
  evenly spaced.
- **Engines:** two to four large bells, ember orange, deep-set.
- **How it breaks:** along the lateral weapon galleries. The hull splits lengthwise between flank casemate runs, and the spire line snaps off as one
  piece. Inside: iron corridors, ember-lit, armored flank gunnery galleries. Breach anchors sit along the flank belt, evenly spaced.
- **Never:** rust (that is the Hullbreakers), blue light, a ram prow shaped like a ship's stem, cathedral windows so literal
  that it reads as another game's ship. The spires are radiators, not steeples: no crosses, no statues.
- **What the present concepts get wrong:** V1b_r_23 is a cathedral on a boat hull (stem bow, stepped decks): keep its mass and
  spire cluster, redraw the hull as a blade. V14_23 has wheel-like pods and red light: ember orange, and pods become radiator
  blocks.

## Meridian Directorate (`hegemony`)

**In one line:** a pale wedge with a line of blue light.

- **Silhouette:** a heavy, thick wedge on twin rails, about 3 : 1, with big shoulder turrets (R183 (3); Ryan on round 4:
  "Hegemony also seems a bit too fragile and slender?"). One low sensor fin, not a tower. Symmetric and identical across the
  fleet: the same parts repeated at different sizes.
- **Shape language:** machined, modular, horizontal. Flush panels, straight seams, repeated modules. The ion weapon is a
  recessed emitter trench in a blunt bow face, never prongs (R183 (1); Ryan: "every ship has the guns directly on the nose
  which feels odd").
- **Colours:** pale grey, steel-blue trim, implant-blue light strips that pulse in time across the whole fleet.
- **Guns sit:** low armoured mounts sunk into the shoulder armour, short thick barrels, never tall round turrets with long
  thin barrels (R185 (4); Ryan: "The hegemony guns look weird and almost cartoonish"); plus the bow emitter trench. Small
  drone bays in the flanks.
- **Engines:** a flat row of rectangular blue-white nozzles.
- **How it breaks:** in modules. It gives way at the bulkhead rings between modules, like a spine coming apart, the rims torn and scorched (R186). Inside:
  white corridors, blue emergency light, racks of identical equipment. Breach anchors sit on the module joints.
- **Never:** rust, asymmetry, ornament, warm light. No yacht decks, no conning tower, no tall mast.
- **What the present concepts get wrong:** H7 to H10 read as yachts or submarines (a tall sail-like tower, stepped cabin
  tiers); H4_11 is a sea battleship with a mast tower. Keep the wedge and the blue lines; flatten the superstructure into one
  low fin and turret rows.

## Ashfall Hullbreakers (`corsair`)

**In one line:** a lopsided brick of rust and stolen plate that runs dark.

- **Silhouette:** blunt, heavy-bowed, uneven. Bigger on one side than the other. Listening dishes and wake-sniffer scoops at
  the bow, boarding claws under it. The one faction allowed to be junky.
- **Shape language:** bolted, patched. Hull plates torn from every other faction, kept in their old colours. Nothing hangs
  off the ship: no loose chains, cages or dangling cargo; trophies and cargo are bolted flat (R185 (3); Ryan: "I don't
  understand the random things hanging off, it reads as naval"). Rocket racks sit on the top deck as big mismatched
  bolted-on launchers (R183 (4); Ryan: "rockets need to be on top to fit the scrapped together theme").
- **Patch size (R252, Ryan, Nov 14: "agree"):** the trophy patches read big like the A20 concept, not small dark plates; still
  uneven in size, rows and offsets (R240). **Their tone (R274, Ryan, Nov 15: "those should be a global rule for all of the bigger
  paler patches too. The white looks unfinished"):** dark grey salvaged metal, clearly lighter than the soot plate, never white or
  chalky; the violet Eclipse trophy plates stay. SUPERSEDED, kept so nobody follows it: "big and pale" (R252's tone, ended by R274). In the stack: `TROPHY` in `tools/blender/kits/hullbreakers/stack.py`
  (issue 726; RECIPE.md, the paint stack).
- **Patchwork cause and repair (R289, issue 875):** A16 and A17 have real mixed-size slabs, varied thickness and stacked
  patches in their design files, on the shared sheet kit's original plater. A18 to A20 selected the later `courses=True`
  builder (issue 633): small rectangular plates in brick rows and stepped terraces. The same paint stack could not remove
  that ordered geometry; R240 changed shader cells, not those slabs. KB1CC already split faces without courses, but its
  shallow slabs, small turns and reduced craft paint wear still read as flat notes. Those four sheets now use `kits/hullbreakers/plating.py`:
  mixed-size cuts across each face, skewed corners, turned and overlapping slabs, thickness steps and welded lap joints.
  Material weights, the trophy share and the R274 dark grey palette stay unchanged. Grey trophies keep their low wear.
  **KB1CC follow-up (R292, issue 875 run 2):** the craft-only palette from issue 853 mapped even `soot` and `soot2` to bright
  red, and its reduced grime and occlusion left broad clean salmon faces. The first repair's thicker relief made the small
  patches look loose. Craft zones now read their colours from the same `CONCEPT` palette as the capitals: dark iron under
  varied rust red, blood red and salvaged plates. Stronger seam occlusion, grime, scuffs and broken edge wear weather the real
  geometry without another tile grid. KB1CC keeps mixed sizes and welded overlaps, with lower relief bedded against the skin.
  Trophy colour and share stay unchanged. A16, A17, capital paint settings and the shared kit stay unchanged,
  including the A16 fixture record. Judge the painted result beside its concept and the accepted capital reference
  (A18 for KB1CC, A16 for the capitals) at the saved
  `paint_full` camera, not by plate counts. Proof and the repeatable bake script are linked in
  `docs/shots/look_bench/hullbreaker_patchwork/README.md`.
- **Colours:** soot black, rust, dried-blood red, patches of trophy colour (dark grey salvaged metal, R274; violet Eclipse plate), dim
  red running lights. No crystal shard: it came off A16 and A17 (R197; Ryan: "Not sure why there is a weird crystal in there
  but we can get rid of that").
- **Guns sit:** wherever they could be bolted: mismatched calibres, off-centre, never facing backward at rest (RULEBOOK 4.2). Casemates in the
  bow, tube racks on the deck.
- **Engines:** mismatched bells with a red-orange glow, one often larger than the rest.
- **How it breaks:** at the seams. Patch plates tear off first, then the hull parts where sections are welded together,
  ragged and uneven, never a clean cut (R186). Inside: scavenged frames, loot holds, kennel decks. One more breach anchor than
  the base count, placed unevenly.
- **Never:** clean symmetry, bright light, fresh paint. And still no sea-ship parts: junk is allowed, a boat is not.
- **What the present concepts get wrong:** all five carry lattice masts, cranes, porthole rows and keel fins (Muse's C15s trial
  shows them plainly). The masts become listening dishes and antenna clusters, the cranes become boarding claws and grapple
  arms, portholes go, and the keel fin becomes a ventral scoop or goes.

## The Glasswrights (`ithar`)

Ryan, Nov 10: "I like the idea-ish but it comes off looking as almost insect like. I think we go with a different idea but in a
similar vane." So the paired wing and petal vanes go. What stays is the idea underneath: a people of optical engineers whose
ships catch, store and release light.

**In one line:** an instrument for light, built as a warship.

- **Who they are (lore 6.1):** the Starwrights who stayed flesh; the finest optical engineers who ever lived. They built the
  collectors, mirrors and beam lines that carried a star's light across a system, and watched that machine kill their sun.
- **A small elite fleet, never a swarm (Ryan, Nov 20, issue 1298).** "Glasswrights aren't supposed to be a swarm faction like
  chorus or even hullbreakers. A little more elite." Few ships, each worth more: balance them with more hull on the
  four fleet hulls (sliver, lancet, prism, aperture; player and enemy copies alike, "so it's consistent"), not with cheaper
  or more numerous ships. The boss, The Unfinished, is not a fleet hull and keeps its own hull (470). They stay
  glassy: no armour added, evasion and shields still carry them.
- **First rule, ahead of any shape rule (R192).** Ryan, Nov 11: "It doesn't match with how I envision the glasswrights being
  artistic, thoughtful in creation and looking to create beauty with function, even in these warships." Every structural
  part is shaped with care and is also the ornament; the weapons are the centrepieces and must make sense.
- **Lenses are grown in (R196).** Ryan: "The lenses are a littlenweird and don't feel naturally ingrained into the ship like
  you'd expect with their lore. It should feel almost seamless and less bolted on. Like a work of art or blown glass, though
  able to rotate, etc." One continuous skin of glass and metal; no pod, bracket, ring mount or visible seam between lens and
  ship. Forward lenses visibly point forward. G17 (clear bubbles) and G18 (cream tubes) failed this (R201, R206).
- **Shape language:** a long leaf of flowing, twisted pearl ribbons (CD5, R298; it grew from the G13 and G15 base). Rigid,

## Eclipse (`deathless`)

Ryan, Nov 10: "Shapes are the biggest issue. They look like just giant spinning tops, at least capital ships." His colour
line that day ("I like the green glow but it should be on brand with eclipse") kept a green corona on the hulls. **Superseded
Nov 20 2026 (issue 1419):** asked "the rim is written as green and the weapons as violet ... my pick is all violet, to match
the deaths and the color file", Ryan answered "yes ... agree with you". Eclipse is all violet: no green on the hulls.

**In one line:** a black shade with a thin ring of violet-white fire at its edge.

- **Who they are (lore 7.1):** the Starwrights who uploaded. Machine bodies in a system they made dark, each with a small core
  of trapped light, all that is left of their sun.
- **The corona:** a thin, cold violet-white line along the rim of every shade plate, white-gold at its hottest arcs, and the
  trapped light core seen through gaps, violet-white grading to violet. Never a pooled glow inside ribs or sockets, which
  reads as undead.
- **Shape language:** sunshades and heat shields: broad layered plates with the ship sheltering behind them. The shade always
  faces the enemy, like a shield held forward. Wide and flat, or a forward-facing arc or ring. The shade sits over the ship
  as a sunshade, the ship's heart and guns under and behind it, as E13 is built (R256, Ryan Nov 15). Guns never fire through
  slots in a shade. E14 is the exception being redesigned: its ring stands upright as in the concept, built around one larger
  gun at its centre, "like a glass cannon" (R256, Ryan Nov 15 07:02).
- **Colours:** dark violet-black plates, the violet-white corona line, a small bright violet-white core, white-gold accents.
  Engines, weapon bolts, damage glow and deaths come from godot/fx/faction_looks.json `deathless`, the one faction colour
  file (issue 1205 removed the all-green hull_table FAC3D override). The Doom gun's `weapon_core` is deep violet too (Ryan
  Nov 21 2026, "Yes make it a violet core", issue 1503; replaces R263's green core): no green is left in that file. The hull paint lives in
  tools/blender/kits/eclipse/stack.py: until that stack is repainted and the hulls rebaked (contrib/opus/plans/eclipse_1419.md),
  the installed E11 to E14 hulls still show the old green corona.
- **Panels (R243, Ryan Nov 13):** precise, dead even, ordered and aligned across hull and shade, with recessed seams and
  slight relief. Keep E11's accepted dark violet-black colour. This is machine precision; the Hullbreakers' irregular
  patchwork is their own. The thin uneven corona must read at camera 170, including E12's ring segments. The core glows
  violet-white (Nov 20, all violet), white-hot only at its very centre, and reads at camera 170.
- **Guns sit (R256, Ryan Nov 15):** clear of the shades: on mounts at the shade's heart or root firing over its plates (E13),
  or at the centre of a ring (E14, being redesigned). This replaces "behind the shade's rim, firing through gaps between plates".
- **Engines:** no flaming bells. An eclipse ring of pale violet light.
- **How it breaks:** in layers. Shade plates peel away band by band, then the body behind is bare. Inside: archive vaults,
  dark decks, the core's light. Breach anchors sit on the shade's bands.
- **Never:** a disc or cone on a vertical spindle (the spinning top), a spire through the centre of a disc, bone, ribs,
  skulls, any green on the hull, glow pooled in hollows, flame.
- **The E14 exception (R256, PR 804):** E14 is the accepted flare redesign, its ring standing upright around one fixed lance through the centre.

## The Chorus (`chorus`)

Ryan, Nov 10, picked every fault at once: "Reads as cartoon bugs or grubs", "Metal bits and wrong colours", "Idea is right,
execution is off" and "Start over with a new idea". So: the idea of grown, living ships stays; the grub is gone.

**In one line:** something vast and eyeless that was grown as a weapon and never stopped growing.

- **Who they are (lore 5.1):** not a people: a weapon the Fleshwrights grew to destroy Eclipse, engineered flesh that lives on
  starlight, eats anything, endures the cold and breeds without end. It consumed its makers and became one swarm with one
  appetite. The Fleshwrights were kin to the Glasswrights, so a Chorus ship may echo a Glasswright shape in flesh.
- **Shape language:** grown, not built. Scale and menace first: slow, heavy, deep-sea. Hide, membrane, chitin ridges, light
  inside the body. Symmetric where a body would be, ragged where it has been scarred and regrown.
- **Colours:** muddy olive-brown hide with dark red veins, pores and wrinkles (never maroon, never "red clay"), chitin a bone to
  horn tone, bile yellow-green light from inside at the veil roots and bile slits. The colour lives in the shared Chorus paint
  stack (tools/blender/kits/chorus/stack.py) and the build sheet's colour notes, not in more image rounds (R204; Ryan: "we can
  fix color ourselves rather than get stuck in a loop with color fixes with image generation"). Veils are satin (roughness
  0.6), not gloss, so they show no white hot spots.
- **Body and armour (R349, Ryan Nov 20; C13 round G accepted in game Nov 20, PR 1308):** a full body of lumpy fused swellings,
  deep folds and wrinkles grown into the skin (kit `body.field`), never a smooth tube with plates on top. Armour is grown
  chitin almost everywhere (Ryan, Nov 20 4:18 PM CT: "cover the chorus ships in armor almost everywhere"): armadillo bands
  that wrap down both flanks to the keel (kit `plates.armadillo`, its default `plates.WRAP`; a sheet never stops them
  higher), banded and ridged, lips aft, hide rolled up into their edges, broken only round the organs; where a fitting cuts
  a band, a half band still grows on its clear side (`fill`), so the shell hugs each fitting. Sacs and pods show dark veins and
  no lit spots at all: each sac's crown is cut open into a dark pore with a bore going down and a fleshy lip, never a round lit window, a glowing slit or
  glowing veins (kit `parts.sac` default window 'slit'; Ryan Nov 20: "random yellow circles on the pods ... looks odd", Nov 21:
  "the same weird yellow circle or patch on the sacs"). Gland vents are real openings: the knoll's crown is cut away under
  the puckered lip and a matte dark bore runs down into it (kit `parts.spinal` style 'gland', zone 'pit'; Ryan Nov 21: "no actual
  holes like the concept", then on dark discs: "these are clearly not holes"). Never a dark disc on a closed dome. An organ whose bore runs down into the body (C14's launch mouths) cuts the hull and any
  band open under it, and keeps the inside rooms clear of the bore (`K.open_hull` with depth, after the armour and rooms; Ryan Nov 21: "There are no actual holes, it's just caps"). A launch
  mouth carries a lobed flesh door, shut between launches, plain flesh, opening from the middle (`launch_mouth(door=6)`, issue
  1543; Ryan Nov 21: "Closer and plain flesh"); the lobes are their own hinged nodes and the game opens them on launch
  (docs/ship_pipeline/HARDPOINTS.md "Doors").
  Flank and brood sacs wear flat chitin caps, two rings of thin plates lying close with the slit open at the crown (kit
  `plates.dome_caps(flat=True)`; Ryan: "caps, but flatter"). The belly is banded too, so `plates.fused_patches` is only for a spot
  the bands cannot reach. No flat stone tiles: the R341 shell (`plates.armour`) is retired for new builds.
  Every Chorus hull uses these kit calls, so a fix in the kit reaches C10 to C14 at once (R333). The grown paint is the
  stack's default for every Chorus ship (a recipe opts out only with "chorus_look": "r341"), and every ship of every faction is
  gated by the stage 5 detail check (issue 1517; ships.md section 0, rule 16). Surface detail must read at
  camera 26 and still give texture at 170; stage 5's detail check (tools/recipe/detail_check.py) fails a flat clay skin.
- **Guns sit:** in throats, spines and sacs: a weapon is an organ. Brood sacs along the flanks for the wings.
- **Engines:** no nozzles. Pulsing vents or trailing membranes with a yellow-green glow.
- **How it breaks:** it bursts and tears. Sacs rupture first, then the body tears open. Inside: flesh and bone (R98), wet and
  lit from within. One more breach anchor than the base count on the big ones.
- **Never:** grub or caterpillar segments, anything cute or round-cheeked, legs, eyes, a face, any metal (no masts, antennas,
  towers or plates), red or magenta flesh.

**The method that works (use it for every later ship; each line names the ruling it comes from).**
1. Write the ship before drawing it: its exact weapons from data.js and where each sits, its engines, its proportions, and the
   thirteen-line gate (docs/playbooks/concepts_round2.md). Round 1 failed because no picture was told how many guns the ship has.
2. Draw in the one concept style (R197). A picture that reads as an illustration, a toy or a cartoon fails, whatever its shape.
   Each faction keeps its own palette and character ("realistic" does not mean rusty).
3. It must read as armed from above at thumbnail size (R176). Each faction mounts its forward weapon its own way, never a long
   barrel on the tip of the nose, and no two factions share an outline from above (R183; gate lines 1 and 8).
4. **When Ryan likes a picture, the next image job edits that picture (R192).** Image to image, the changes listed, everything
   else untouched; a result that drifted in mass, silhouette or character fails. Ryan: "Can we use our prior concept from
   before all these rounds as the base? Or just use that?" Six Hullbreaker rounds were lost redescribing a liked picture in
   words.
5. **Colour alone never sends a picture back (R204).** Colour is fixed in the build.
6. **When image rounds cannot reach the style without breaking the shape, stop the image rounds** and send the shape through
   the Opus build-sheet route (R204 (3), R206 (2)): a blockout locked to the liked shape, dressed in the style.
7. **The accepted picture guides the build; it is not traced (R207, R213).** Ryan: "Use it to guide, not the very final exact
   design." And: "The concept should inform and guide but it's not a final play by play guide." The Opus builder is the
   designer of record: it keeps the picture's identity (mass, outline from above, character, palette, where the big features
   sit), fixes what would not work as a built object, takes guns from data.js slots as batteries that make sense, and lists
   every change with its reason on the build sheet.
8. **Start from what was already liked (R180), and find it first (R196).** When Ryan points at a picture from memory, find it,

9. Check every feature under the battle camera before briefing it (R183), and run the naval pass on every sheet, side view
   first (R185; gate line 11). Image models drift to sea ships whenever a brief says "deck", "hull", "prow" or "barge": use

10. Put the code name on every picture sent to Ryan (R185: "I can't tell which one is a11").
11. The Board reviews every sheet against the gate before Ryan sees it, and says plainly which fail.
